sector: Independent fine-jewellery house, made to order and sold by appointment, with a small stockist channel.
founded_place_size: Founded 2014, in a room above a bookshop in Montreal, Quebec. Four people, one bench.
about: Maison Valcere is a four-person high-jewellery house working to order for marriages and milestones. Twenty two references sit in the current book, most cut and set in-house and shown by appointment above the shop. The house sells quiet, considered pieces to clients who return once a decade, not once a season.
audience: Clients aged 35 to 60 buying for a marriage or a milestone, plus a short list of premium stockists. Considered, appointment-led buyers who research before they visit and expect the metal, stone and carat answered without asking.
price_positioning: Pieces run 900 to 6,500 dollars, positioned as appointment fine jewellery well above a mall counter and just below the named international maisons. Price is shown discreetly or not at all; the room and the book carry the value.

palette.name: House Black
palette.usage: The house name, headings and body text on Bench Ivory, as the piece name and spec lines on valcere_spec_card_PRINT.pdf and the wordmark in valcere_copy.txt; the only dark ground, which the reversed wordmark sits on.

palette.name: Bench Ivory
palette.role: mandatory for any light ground or panel; the only light ground permitted
palette.usage: The light ground for pages and panels, as on valcere_spec_card_PRINT.pdf, and the ground the wordmark sits on in House Black. Never a type colour.

palette.name: Signature White
palette.role: mandatory where type is reversed on House Black
palette.usage: Type reversed out of House Black, the wordmark included, as valcere_copy.txt sets it. Never a ground or panel.

palette.name: Fine Grey
palette.usage: Reference codes, small labels and fine print on Bench Ivory, as the reference line on valcere_spec_card_PRINT.pdf. Never a ground, a panel, the house name or body text.

palette.name: Warm Gold
palette.usage: Hairline rules only, as the single rule on valcere_spec_card_PRINT.pdf. Never type, a ground, a panel or a fill.

typography: Maison Valcère runs on Cormorant Garamond for display and Apercu for text, quoted at deck size. Step 01, display, is the house name in Cormorant Garamond Light 300 caps at 44 pt on 48 pt leading tracked 160 units, always stacked, MAISON over VALCÈRE, with the lower line letterspaced to the exact width of the upper so the pair locks into one hairline block and the grave accent stays intact; the same block sets at 96 pt on the A2 poster and 64 px on the feed ad. Step 02, subheading, is Cormorant Garamond Light 300 caps at 22 pt on 26 pt leading tracked 120 units, exactly half the deck display and the only size invented here. Step 03, body, is Apercu Regular at 11 pt on 16 pt leading, tracking zero, set to a maximum of 65 characters, and 22 px on 32 px leading on screen. Step 04, fine print, is Apercu Regular at 8.5 pt on 13 pt leading tracked 20 units. Nothing in display is ever heavier than Light, and Apercu carries every figure, carat, reference and millimetre.
voice: Plain, precise, never salesy. States materials and provenance and stops. Example line: "Eighteen karat white gold, set with a single old-cut stone, made to your hand."
brand_assets_status: The original wordmark artwork left with the designer who set it a decade ago. The only surviving version is a photograph of an old printed swing tag, so the mark has to be recovered from that before it can be used again. No usable logo files, colour references or type spec survive; these guidelines are being reconstructed this season.
values: One object per canvas, honest materials, and a mark that reads as ours at every size. Restraint is the house, not decoration.

type_system.signature_move: The house name always stacks on two lines, MAISON over VALCÈRE, in Cormorant Garamond Light caps tracked 160 units, with the second line letterspaced to the exact width of the first so the pair locks into one hairline block.
rules: Never set the house name on one line. MAISON always stacks over VALCÈRE.
The lower line is letterspaced to the exact width of the upper so the two lock into one hairline block.
The grave accent on VALCÈRE stays intact at every size.
Never set display heavier than Light 300.
Display holds at 44 pt in the deck, 96 pt on the A2 poster and 64 px on the feed ad.
Apercu Regular sets specifications and carries every figure, carat, reference and millimetre.
Price is shown discreetly or not at all.
The 22 pt subheading is the one size not already stated in the spec, set at exactly half the deck display.

palette_rules.distribution: Grounds and panels are Bench Ivory or House Black and nothing else. On Bench Ivory, the house name, headings and body text are House Black, and reference codes, labels and fine print may be Fine Grey, as on valcere_spec_card_PRINT.pdf. On House Black, all type is Signature White, as the reversed wordmark in valcere_copy.txt. The wordmark is House Black on Bench Ivory or Signature White on House Black only. Warm Gold is for hairline rules only. Fine Grey and Warm Gold together cover no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity, as on the house's own spec card. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, and no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over a photograph: type sits on a solid ground or on a solid panel beside or over the photograph.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the five palette hexes for type, grounds, panels, rules, buttons or icons. No Warm Gold, gold, metallic, foil or glow effect on any type, and no icon, symbol or ornament: the identity is purely typographic (valcere_copy.txt).
palette_rules.photography: Photographs keep their own corrected colour and are never recoloured toward the palette: the bench sweep is not tinted Bench Ivory, yellow gold is not pushed toward Warm Gold, and the sapphire, emerald, ruby and aquamarine keep their own hue.
